paper.title: Multimodal Emotion Recognition using Audio-Video Transformer Fusion with Cross Attention

summarization.summary: This paper addresses multimodal emotion recognition by proposing the Audio-Video Transformer Fusion with Cross Attention (AVT-CA) model, which utilizes a dual-channel architecture to process spectral-temporal audio cues and micro-expressions via Conv2D. The methodology employs transformer-based cross-modal interaction with adaptive modality weighting to mitigate temporal misalignment across disparate sampling rates. Experiments on RAVDESS, CMU-MOSEI, and CREMA-D demonstrate state-of-the-art performance, achieving 96.11% accuracy and 93.78% F1-score on RAVDESS, 95.84% accuracy on CMU-MOSEI, and 94.13% accuracy on CREMA-D. Ablation studies confirm that increasing attention heads from one to four yields significant gains, with the full model providing approximately a 20% improvement over ablated components. However, the study acknowledges limitations including reliance on specific datasets, sensitivity to noisy inputs, and unreported generalization gaps. Furthermore, the scarcity of language-based transcriptions introduces uncertainty in real-world pipelines, and the lack of explicit quantification for some reviewed architectures suggests potential gaps in comparative analysis.

factual_consistency.reason: The central AVT-CA architecture, cross-modal fusion approach, Conv2D-based visual processing, and all reported benchmark figures match the source: RAVDESS 96.11% accuracy and 93.78% F1, CMU-MOSEI 95.84% accuracy, and CREMA-D 94.13% accuracy. The study discusses an approximately 20% gain for the combined model, but the summary risks attributing this to increasing attention heads alone; the per-component ablation changes are smaller or mixed depending on dataset. Text-transcription scarcity appears as background motivation rather than an experimentally demonstrated deployment limitation.
